original_question: Design a Verilog module named `pipereg_w32`. This module should function as a 32-bit pipeline register. It should operate synchronously on the positive edge of the `clk` input. The module needs an active-low synchronous reset input, `resetn`, which forces the output `q` to zero. It also requires an active-low synchronous squash input, `squashn`, which likewise forces the output `q` to zero. The reset and squash signals should take precedence over normal data loading. When neither the reset nor the squash is active, the register should load the 32-bit input `d` into the output `q` only when the active-high enable signal `en` is high. If `en` is low and neither reset nor squash is active, the output `q` should retain its current value. Define the module interface exactly as follows: inputs `clk`, `resetn`, `en`, `squashn`, `d [31:0]` and output `q [31:0]`.
